topic: DOJ-wide budget cuts and prioritized restoration requests
summary: Chair Mika Suansing raised the broad distribution of DOJ budget cuts and asked the department to identify which reductions should be restored first. The DOJ official detailed Bureau of Immigration reductions, including about 673 million in MOE as spoken, multiple ICT and building-related amounts, and a total requirement characterized by the chair as more than 1.1 billion to 1.2 billion. NBI Director Melvin identified hazard pay, operations, vehicles, administrative capability, and cybercrime laboratories and equipment as priorities, citing a proposed increase from 4,000 to 15,000 and a monthly operating figure of 44,000,000,000 whose context was unclear. The chair also catalogued percentage reductions across anti-trafficking, OSIIC, anti-cybercrime, corrections, legal services, and several attached agencies. DOJ officials committed to submit a consolidated, prioritized list within the week and consult the attached agencies. The committee had not approved specific restorations, and the vice chair solicited a motion to terminate the budget briefing.
question: The committee sought to identify which DOJ-wide budget reductions affected priority programs and to obtain a consolidated, agency-ranked list of items for possible restoration. It also asked specific agencies to explain the components of their cuts and their most urgent funding needs.
agency_position: The DOJ and its attached agencies maintained that multiple priority programs and operational requirements had been reduced across the department. DOJ officials agreed to consolidate the requests, consult the attached agencies, and rank the restoration items by priority.
outcome: The DOJ committed to submit a comprehensive prioritized restoration list for consolidation and review by the committee. No final restoration amounts were approved during this exchange; the budget briefing was being brought to termination.

positions.position: The committee should not attempt to restore every reduction because fiscal space was limited; instead, the DOJ should rationalize and prioritize the most essential requests across all attached agencies.
NBI priorities included higher agents' hazard pay, operating funds, administrative-capability improvements, additional vehicles, cybercrime tools, equipment, and regional cybercrime laboratories.
The DOJ would submit a consolidated, agency-by-agency restoration wish list with an order of prioritization.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: Chair Mika Suansing said the deliberation ultimately concerned the DOJ's budgetary requirements and that she was reviewing maintenance and other operating expenses, capital outlay, and agency-level allocations.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She identified the Bureau of Immigration as a major concern, including its locally funded ICT project and maintenance and other operating expenses, and asked which specific components had been reduced so the committee could determine what might need restoration.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: The official identified the Bureau of Immigration reductions, including MOE of R673 million 476,000; a drug-free workplace initiative of RM3413000; additional MOE for the expanded alien registration system; and the Paragon budget of NZD8871000.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: The official added MMOE of 651,202,000 for locally funded ICT-system and infrastructure projects.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: For capital outlay, the official cited 27,811,000 for locally funded ICT-system and infrastructure projects, N951.531 million for the main and support offices nationwide, and R276.280 million for post-construction of the BI building.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: Chair Suansing said the Bureau of Immigration alone represented a substantive restoration requirement and that, given limited fiscal space, the committee would have to prioritize the items to restore.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She characterized the Bureau of Immigration requirement as over 1,100,000,000, later referring to 1,200,000,000 and an ICT system requirement of one plus billion.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She said the DOJ should provide one consolidated list covering its attached agencies, and that the committee would review the list and prioritize requests among those agencies.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: The official agreed to submit a wish list with the corresponding order of prioritization and to consult the various DOJ agencies.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: Chair Suansing said the DOJ-wide review showed that the reductions were not confined to the Bureau of Immigration but occurred across the department and its attached agencies.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She pointed to cuts in law-enforcement priorities, including anti-trafficking enforcement and OSIIC, and sought the agencies' prioritization of those affected programs.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: The DOJ official responded, "We will put them in the priority," referring to the affected law-enforcement programs.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She noted a cut of over half in victims compensation services and then asked NBI Director Melvin to explain which general administration and support services items had been reduced.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin
thread.said: Director Melvin said there were six items to address. His first priority was increasing agents' hazard pay from 4,000 to 15,000 to bring it in line with other law-enforcement personnel, citing the difficulty of transfers between provinces.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin
thread.said: He said the NBI was conducting about 200 to two twenty operations per month involving financial scams, cybercrime, and related matters, and needed additional funding for operational expenses.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin
thread.said: Director Melvin said operating expenses averaged a minimum of 100 per operation and referred to 44,000,000,000 a month to continue the NBI's activities; the unit of the figures was unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin
thread.said: He also identified administrative-capability improvements, ISO activities, and additional vehicles as priorities, explaining that marked or red-plate vehicles could not be used for undercover operations.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin
thread.said: Director Melvin acknowledged prior-year budget-utilization concerns but said the NBI needed to respond to its congressional mandate, particularly on cybercrime. He said about 80% of crimes were cyber-related and that the NBI wanted regional cybercrime laboratories, tools, and equipment.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: Chair Suansing summarized additional reductions: anti-trafficking enforcement had fallen 41%, OSIIC 59%, and anti-cybercrime 71%; she also cited cuts in corrections, legal services, immigration, LRA, OGCC, OSG, PPA, PCGG, and OADR programs.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She said the reductions were broad-based, including 15% for the refugee and stateless persons protection unit, 13% for the cited Subucor program, 12% for LRA general administration and support services, 8% for OSG operations, 36% for PPA general administration and support services, and 64% for PCGG excluding RLIP and the special account.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: Chair Suansing said the committee would work with Vice Chair Mike Tan and the DOJ to prioritize restoration items through the budget amendments review subcommittee, which would examine proposed amendments line by line.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: She requested that the DOJ submit its prioritized list within the week, preferably as soon as possible, so the committee could consolidate the requests before the BARC deliberation.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: The DOJ official agreed to comply and submit a comprehensive listing with the appropriate prioritization for each agency.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: Chair Suansing said she would defer to Vice Chair Mike on any further exchanges before the prioritized list was finalized and emphasized that restoration decisions would have to account for limited fiscal space.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Mike Tan
thread.said: The vice chair thanked Chair Suansing and solicited a motion to terminate the budget briefing of the DOJ and its attached agencies.

topic: Bureau of Immigration general administration and support funding
summary: Chair Mika Suansing asked which Bureau of Immigration general administration and support components had been reduced. A DOJ official identified operating and capital-outlay items, including ICT systems, support-office facilities, and post-construction of the BI building. The listed figures included about 673 million for maintenance and other operating expenses, 651,202,000 for locally funded ICT operating expenses, 27,811,000 for ICT capital outlay, and N951.531 million for the main and support offices, although several transcript amounts contained unclear currency labels. The chair characterized the overall BI reduction as over 1,000,000,000 and said restoration would have to be prioritized across the DOJ. The DOJ committed to consult the attached agencies and submit a comprehensive, prioritized restoration list within the week.
question: The committee sought to identify which Bureau of Immigration general administration and support components had been reduced and which items might warrant restoration. It also sought a prioritized list from the DOJ and its attached agencies in light of limited fiscal space.
agency_position: The DOJ official identified the Bureau of Immigration's reduced operating and capital-outlay components, including ICT systems, support-office facilities, and the post-construction of a BI building. The DOJ undertook to consult the attached agencies and submit a comprehensive, prioritized restoration list.
outcome: The Bureau of Immigration's reduced components were identified, but no restoration was approved during the discussion. The matter moved forward through the DOJ's commitment to submit a prioritized list for later committee consideration.

positions.position: The Bureau of Immigration reductions were substantial and should be reviewed for possible restoration, but requests had to be prioritized across the DOJ because fiscal space was limited.

topic: NBI general administration, support services, and operations funding
summary: Mika Suansing asked Director Melvin to explain the NBI's 42% cut to general administration and support services. Director Melvin identified higher agent hazard pay, operational expenses, administrative capability, additional vehicles, and cybercrime laboratories, tools, and equipment as restoration needs. He cited increasing hazard pay from 4,000 to 15,000, about 200 to two twenty operations per month, a minimum 100 average expense per operation, and a stated 44,000,000,000 a month requirement whose currency and calculation were unclear. He also said 80% of crimes were related to cybercrime and that the anti-cybercrime item had been cut by 71%. The DOJ committed to submit a comprehensive, prioritized list of restoration requests after consulting its attached agencies. No specific NBI amount was restored during the hearing.
question: The committee sought to establish which NBI general administration and support services items had been cut and which restoration requests should be prioritized. It also sought the NBI's operational justification for additional funding, particularly for personnel support, investigations, vehicles, and cybercrime capabilities.
agency_position: The NBI said its 42% cut to general administration and support services affected resources needed for higher agent hazard pay, frequent operations, operational expenses, administrative capability, vehicles, and cybercrime tools and facilities. Director Melvin maintained that additional funding was necessary to sustain the bureau's investigations and build regional cybercrime laboratory capacity, while acknowledging prior-year budget-utilization issues.
outcome: The NBI identified its principal restoration needs, but no specific restoration amount was approved or restored during the discussion. The issue was committed to the DOJ's submission of a prioritized list for subsequent committee review.

positions.position: She viewed the NBI's support-services and anti-cybercrime cuts as priorities for review and sought an agency-ranked list of restoration needs, subject to limited fiscal space.
He supported restoring or increasing funding for agent hazard pay, investigative operations, vehicles, administrative capability, and cybercrime laboratories, tools, and equipment.

topic: PCGG mandate and recovery of hidden wealth, including the PHP70 billion target
summary: A committee member questioned the agency about recovered hidden wealth, remaining assets, and the pending cases. The agency said about 67 cases were pending in the appellate courts and referred to more than PHP70 billion, which the member identified as the target and the agency confirmed. The agency said the PCGG was attached to the Department of Justice and had operated independently without pressure. It also discussed replacing or succeeding the PCGG with a body empowered to pursue unlawfully acquired assets of all public officials under RA thirteen seventy nine. The agency explained the summary judgment process and reported that the government had won an appeal in New York involving enforcement of the Swiss accounts judgment, subject to possible US Supreme Court action. The committee requested a report, which it said it looked forward to receiving.
question: The committee sought to establish what hidden wealth had been recovered, what assets and cases remained pending, and whether the PHP70 billion figure was a recovery target. It also examined the PCGG’s institutional status, independence, and a proposed expansion of its forfeiture mandate.
agency_position: The agency said recoveries had been made through summary judgment, compromise agreements, and other cases, but some assets and cases remained unresolved because entities were unregistered or nonoperational and witnesses were unavailable. It supported an expanded forfeiture mandate covering unlawfully acquired assets of all public officials and maintained that it had acted independently without pressure.
outcome: The agency answered the committee’s questions and undertook to provide the requested report. The recovery figures and the proposed expanded mandate were discussed, but the remaining assets and appellate cases were not resolved during the exchange.

positions.position: The member sought a report on recovered hidden wealth and clarification of the more than PHP70 billion figure, the PCGG’s attachment to the Department of Justice, and the legal basis and operation of summary judgment.

topic: Civil forfeiture authority and the Swiss accounts case
summary: A committee member asked the DOJ about recovered hidden wealth, remaining assets, and pending cases involving the Arelma and Swiss accounts matters. The DOJ said some assets had been recovered through summary judgment, compromise agreements, and other cases, but some investigations could not proceed because corporations were unregistered or nonoperational and witnesses were unavailable. It reported about 67 cases pending in appellate courts involving more than PHP70 billion, which the member restated as the target. The DOJ also described a proposed successor to the PCGG with authority to pursue civil forfeiture against public officials whose assets were disproportionate to legitimate income. On the Swiss accounts case, it said the government had won an appeal in New York and was awaiting possible US Supreme Court action. The committee requested a report on recovered hidden wealth, which was expected to be provided.

It supported an expanded successor agency to the PCGG and said the Swiss accounts case had been favorably decided on appeal but remained subject to possible US Supreme Court action.
outcome: The DOJ explained the recovery mechanisms, reported about 67 appellate cases involving more than PHP70 billion, and clarified that the Swiss accounts appeal had been won but remained subject to possible US Supreme Court action. A report on recovered hidden wealth was requested and left as a forthcoming submission.

thread.speaker: a DOJ official
thread.said: The official stated that the DOJ had not been pressured by the President or the President's family and had performed its duties independently.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member restated the matter as a PHP70 billion target involving ill-gotten wealth in pending cases.

thread.speaker: a DOJ official
thread.said: The official discussed creating a new agency to take over the mandate of the PCGG, with an expanded mandate applicable to all public officials who had unlawfully acquired assets, rather than being limited to the Marcos matter.

thread.speaker: a DOJ official
thread.said: The official said the expanded authority would allow the filing of civil forfeiture cases under RA thirteen seventy nine. Where a public official's assets were manifestly disproportionate to salary and other legitimate income, the law provided a presumption that shifted the burden to the official to explain the accumulation.

thread.speaker: a DOJ official
thread.said: The official contrasted civil forfeiture with a criminal case: summary judgment was based on the pleadings, while a criminal case required proof beyond reasonable doubt and a paper trail showing that the assets came from government funds.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member asked for a further explanation of summary judgment and initially asked whether it involved foreign courts.

thread.speaker: a DOJ official
thread.said: The official clarified that the summary judgment was by local courts, not foreign courts.

thread.speaker: a DOJ official
thread.said: Regarding the Swiss accounts matter, the official said the Philippine government had filed a petition in New York for forfeiture and enforcement of a foreign judgment. The government had recently won an appeal and was awaiting action by the US Supreme Court on whether it would affirm the New York Court of Appeals decision.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member said the committee looked forward to receiving the requested report and thanked the Chair.
